name: Decency and Respect
definition: No matter how brilliant someone may be, there's no place in our Dream Team for people who don't treat their colleagues with decency and respect.

rows.situation: A brilliant person who treats colleagues badly
rows.under: Protects them because the output is strong.
rows.justRight: Says the treatment is the problem, gives them a real chance to change, and parts ways if they will not.
rows.over: Removes them on a rumor, or for a style that is merely different, and calls it decency.

rows.situation: A hard disagreement about the work
rows.justRight: Stays on the work, assumes good intent, and still says the disagreement clearly.
rows.over: Avoids the disagreement so nobody feels disrespected, and the wrong call stands.

rows.situation: A colleague whose background or manner is not yours
rows.under: Treats the difference as a reason to discount them.
rows.justRight: Respects the difference and still holds the same bar for the work.
rows.over: Refuses to give them direct feedback, and calls the silence respect.

rows.situation: A tense moment where you do not yet know why someone did something
rows.under: Assigns the worst motive and acts on it.
rows.justRight: Assumes good intent, asks, and changes your view if the facts say otherwise.
rows.over: Assumes good intent so thoroughly that you ignore a pattern of harm.

rows.situation: You have the stronger argument and the room knows it
rows.under: Uses the win to humiliate the person who lost.
rows.justRight: Makes the point, leaves them a way to commit, and does not make them pay socially.
rows.over: Softens a true point so far that the room thinks you changed your mind.
